title: Thoryn provisioning fix request (thoryn-provision-request.json)
description: SSO-3710 (epic SSO-3304; oauthy ADR 2026-10-15-missing-rights-fix-path-cli-and-web-consent §1) — the ONE file a red provisioning job writes (`thoryn login --connection --fix-request <file>` on an invalid_client refusal whose only local mismatch is the GitHub environment; `thoryn provision plan|apply --fix-request <file>` on a plan with access_* rows) and uploads as the run artifact `thoryn-provision-request`. It names every RIGHT the repository's identity is missing and the exact CLI command a WORKSPACE ADMIN runs to grant it. It is a HYPOTHESIS, never a credential: a consumer (the Thoryn GitHub App, SSO-3711/3712) takes repository ids, run id and head sha from GitHub's own workflow_run record and DISCARDS the copies carried here; it re-reads the declared .thoryn/ file at the run's head sha and matches the trust on its pins, never on `trust.name`. Nothing in this file grants anything. It carries no secret: ids, names, commands. The `cli` string of each item is the SAME text the CLI prints on stderr — one rendering, in the CLI.

cliVersion.description: The `thoryn` CLI that wrote the file (`thoryn --version`), or null when unknown.

repository.description: The repository the job ran for — from the job's OIDC claims (`repository`, `repository_id`, `repository_owner_id`) at sign-in, from the runner's `GITHUB_REPOSITORY*` variables at plan time. A HINT: the consumer binds to GitHub's record of the run, not to these.

run.description: The run (`GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_SHA`) and the GitHub environment the job declared (the OIDC token's `environment` claim). A HINT, rebound by the consumer.

workspace.description: The workspace slug the identity signs in to (connection.json `workspace.slug`; the session's workspace at plan time).

file.description: `provision plan|apply` only: the provisioning file that was planned, as given, and its `sha256:` digest — so the consumer re-reads it at the run's head sha and drops any item naming an object the file does not declare. Null for a sign-in refusal.

trust.description: The workload identity trust the identity presents. `clientId` is the trust's `wi_…` workload client (known from the connection or the session); `plane` the environment the trust lives in (`production` for the plane without one); `applyEnvironment` the GitHub environment the trust pins for apply when known; `name` and `id` only when the producer could resolve them (a refused sign-in holds no token, so both are null there; a plan session resolves them when it may list trusts). The consumer matches the trust on PINS against GitHub's record of the run — the name is a hint to disambiguate, never the key.

missing.description: The rights that are missing, one item per refused row (or the one plan_profile item of a refused sign-in). Empty when every failed row is a file fix (see `notes`).

notes.description: Failed rows that are NOT a missing right — the FILE must change (a differing read-only reference, a trust the file cannot declare, a scope the identity does not hold, a create whose parent is the workspace) — so the request says so instead of staying silent.

kind.description: The ADR's grantable set, nothing else: `plan_profile` — a plan profile on the trust for the environment the job ran in (`thoryn workload-identity trusts set-plan-profile`); `owner` — the platform owner relation on an EXISTING object the file declares (access_not_owned on a live id; access_read_only when the identity may only view a resource it is to own; access_owned_elsewhere — then with `cli` null, a dispute an admin decides); `manager` — on the parent `environment:<id>` of a refused create (never on the workspace); `viewer` — on an existing object declared `readOnly: true` the identity holds no relation on.

object.description: The platform object: `application:<clientId>`, `environment:<id>`, `custom_domain:<workspaceId>`, …, or `trust:<name>` for a plan_profile when the trust is named; null when unknown.

subject.description: The identity to grant the right to — the session's `client:<wi_…>`; null for a plan_profile (set on the trust, not granted to a subject) or when the session token was opaque.

environment.description: plan_profile only: the GitHub environment the job ran in — the one the profile is for.

reason.description: Why the right is missing: the engine's row reason (`<code> — …`) or the sign-in's local finding. Names objects and environments, never a secret and never another repository's identity.

cli.description: The exact command a workspace admin runs — the copy-pasteable block the check run relays verbatim and the CLI prints itself. `<trust-id>` where the producer could not resolve the id (`thoryn workload-identity trusts list` shows it); `<subject>` when the session token was opaque. Null for a dispute the CLI shows but never resolves (an object another repository owns).
